newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian silver slightly down at close, gold steady.
newsitem.headline: Indian silver slightly down at close, gold steady.

text.p: Silver prices opened higher amid restricted arrivals but demand resistance at the higher level coupled with light profit-taking trimmed early gains towards the close on Tuesday, dealers said.
"Reports of a modest slide in the world market later on also capped early price rise," one dealer said.
"Sentiment at the close however remained firm amid shortage of ready stock and scattered inflow. Silver may look up again," one broker said.
Gold on the other hand opened higher but remained steady at that level during the day amid limited activity.
Gold was up 15 rupees per 10 gramme on Monday. Prices of a gold biscuit (116.50 gramme) settled 100 rupees higher at 60,400 rupees per piece. They were up 50 rupees each on Monday.
"Physical buying for gold remained low today but traders expect higher demand ahead of the Diwali festival," he said.
